tool_args.rationale: Long-horizon observations at H=15.5 and 21.9 are negative while short-window observations are positive, strongly identifying slow endogenous adaptation opposed to a fast positive sink-coupled response. Fit the specified five parameters numerically to all eight paid rows; the long-horizon probe removes the key forecast ambiguity.

considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: Already acquired; it produced three long-horizon rows including clear sign reversal, resolving the short-horizon ambiguity.
The available eight rows support the identified five-parameter horizon-and-sink model; ODE-specific trajectory data are not needed.
They cannot explain the observed change from positive short/intermediate outputs to negative outputs at long horizons.
The broad variation in s_grad and the supplied sink-gradient signature favor retaining the explicit inhibition factor.
